title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 28
paragraphs: From there Histiaeus made an expedition against Thasos, taking with him a large force of Ionians and Aeolians; and while he was encamped around the town of Thasos, a report came to him that the Phoenicians were sailing up from Miletus to conquer the rest of Ionia. Being informed of this, he left Thasos unconquered and himself hurried to Lesbos, taking his whole army with him. Then, as his army was short of food, he crossed over from Lesbos to reap the corn at Atarneus and also in the plain of the Caicus, which belonged to the Mysians. In these parts there happened to be a Persian named Harpagus commanding a considerable force; and this man fought a battle with him after he had landed, and took Histiaeus himself prisoner and destroyed the greater part of his army.
